Aug 19 (Day 173): Brent rose toward $92/bbl, extending gains for a fourth straight session, after the UAE suspended trade with Iran over alleged missile fire, three China-linked supertankers turned back mid-transit, and the bulker Minoan Dignity was struck near the Strait of Hormuz. Jul 16 (Day 139): Brent ~$84.63/bbl (TradingEconomics), up 6.39% month-over-month as fighting resumed Jul 6-16. Jul 10: ~$76.80/bbl low. Jun 19 (Day 112): ~$80.57/bbl after Geneva/Lucerne talks postponed. Jun 6-7 (Day 99-100): ~$97/bbl peak on drone/missile exchange. Pre-war baseline Feb 27: $77.74/bbl.

label: Hormuz Corridor Status
deltaNote: Aug 26 (Day 180): Iran and Oman agreed a temporary ~7-mile-wide joint navigation corridor through the Strait of Hormuz plus a mine-clearing project, with 30-60 days of further talks toward a permanent route — the first concrete easing of the Hormuz blockade since the June MOU's safe-passage window lapsed in mid-August. Iran says full reopening still requires US sanctions relief and release of frozen assets; commercial shipping has not yet resumed and no timeline for first transits has been announced.
